newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans called steady to five cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans called steady to five cents higher.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were mostly called to open steady to five cents up on dry weather in portions of the Midwest soybean growing area, traders said.
"The rains still are north of the dry areas," a trader said.
There were some calls for a 10-cent-per-bushel higher open in November soybeans but nearby August was seen steady to firm at best with a few calls for a two-cent lower open in that month.
Increased farmer selling and lower cash basis markets continued to weigh on the nearby months.
USDA's weekly export sales report was supportive for old crop soybeans and mildly bearish for new crop.

USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of old crop soy during the week ended July 24 totalled 125,300 tonnes, above expectations for 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes. New crop sales totalled 195,400 tonnes, below expectations for 250,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
As expected, there were no soybeans posted Thursday for delivery on the August contract. Thursday was first notice day for deliveries on the August soy complex futures.
CBOT's Project A overnight trend for soybeans was 1/2 cent lower to 4-1/2 cents higher.
